sources.title: RIT CSCI-539 Seminar in Artificial Intelligence catalog description
sources.author: Rochester Institute of Technology
sources.content: This course examines current topics in Artificial Intelligence. This is intended to allow faculty to pilot potential new undergraduate offerings. Specific course details (such as prerequisites, course seminar, format, learning outcomes, assessment methods, and resource needs) will be determined by the faculty member(s) who propose a specific seminar course in this area. Specific course instances will be identified as belonging to the Artificial Intelligence cluster, the Computer Graphics and Visualization cluster, the Security cluster, or some combination of these three clusters. Contact Hours: Lecture 3

sources.title: scikit-learn User Guide
sources.author: scikit-learn developers
sources.content: Machine-learning workflows separate data preparation, training, validation, testing, model selection, and evaluation. Supervised methods learn a mapping from examples paired with target labels. Unsupervised methods identify structure without target labels. Preprocessing must be fitted only on permitted training data to avoid leakage. Pipelines combine preprocessing and estimators so the same transformations are applied consistently. Cross-validation repeats training and validation across defined data splits. Evaluation metrics must match the task and the cost of different errors. Hyperparameter selection must remain separate from final test evaluation. Leakage, distribution shift, overfitting, and unexamined assumptions can invalidate results.

sources.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
sources.author: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.content: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework organizes work around Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage. Govern establishes policies, responsibilities, and accountability for AI risk. Map documents context, intended use, affected people, and potential impacts. Measure uses qualitative and quantitative methods to analyze identified risks. Manage prioritizes risks and allocates resources for response and monitoring. Risk analysis considers data quality and uncertainty. It also considers robustness, privacy, security, transparency, and fairness. Monitoring continues after deployment because context and system behavior can change.
